ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the circuit in the figure is powered by the voltage source Vsource on the left; the upper end of the power source passes through a series resistor labeled Rseries = 470 Ω to reach the output node; this node is connected downward in parallel through a Zener diode labeled Vz = 5.1 V to ground, while on the right there is also a load resistor labeled Rload = 6 kΩ connected to ground. Then reason: given Vsource = 15 V, and according to the method assume that the Zener diode is in the voltage-regulating state, so the output node voltage is 5.1 V. The series resistor current is (15 - 5.1) / 470 = 9.9 / 470 = 0.0210638 A = 21.0638 mA. The load current is 5.1 / 6000 = 0.00085 A = 0.85 mA. The Zener current equals the series current minus the load current, namely 21.0638 - 0.85 = 20.2138 mA, approximately 20.21 mA.

method.method_draft: First describe the image circuit and identify the zener terminals as the output node to ground. Remove the zener conceptually and form the Thevenin equivalent of the remaining 15 V source, 470 Ω series resistor, and 6 kΩ load: calculate the open-circuit node voltage using the divider and calculate Rth as 470 Ω in parallel with 6 kΩ after shorting the ideal voltage source. method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The circuit image shows a 15 V source on the left feeding a top series resistor labeled R_series = 470 Ω. After this resistor there is a top output node. From that node, a zener diode labeled Vz = 5.1 V is connected down to ground, and a load resistor labeled R_load = 6 kΩ is also connected from the same node down to ground. Thus the zener terminals are the output node and ground.

Reasoning following the assigned method: Conceptually remove the zener diode and find the Thevenin equivalent seen from the output node to ground. The open-circuit node voltage is the divider voltage across the 6 kΩ load: Vth = 15 × 6000 / (470 + 6000) = 13.910 V. With the ideal source shorted, the Thevenin resistance is Rth = 470 Ω || 6000 Ω = (470 × 6000) / (470 + 6000) = 435.86 Ω. Since Vth = 13.910 V is greater than the zener voltage 5.1 V, the zener conducts. Therefore Izener = (Vth − 5.1) / Rth = (13.910 − 5.1) / 435.86 = 0.02021 A = 20.21 mA.
